correctness.rationale: For the displayed specialization, the scalar orthogonal Perry correction is identically zero when E(y) is nonzero. With E(z) nonzero the projection multiplier times E(z) equals y-z, so zero inertia gives s=gamma*tau*d and p=a*s. The stated raw quotient simplifies to -Gamma*s/(tau*zeta*y)=gamma*a. A nonterminal k=1 update therefore first locks Gamma_2 under the strict retention condition; k=0 is not covered. In the locked map with first trial 1, 1<=zeta<=5/4<gamma; for y nonzero one can divide the sufficient acceptance inequality by the positive a*zeta*y^2*(1-zeta/gamma)/gamma. Since the right-hand minimum is at most nu*|E(z)|, it suffices that |y|<=gamma/(sigma*nu*zeta). The first unit update reduces |y| by at least a factor of four (or already hits zero) and resets zeta to 1, so another accepted unit update hits zero. The state recurrence, not the line search globally, is slope-free: outside the sufficient basin acceptance can still depend on a. My exact rational replay (branches/independent_small_replays.py perry) gives Gamma=28/15, states 1,-1/4,0 and nonzero trial points 3/28,-1/14. This checks the stated equations, not a reconstruction of the complete implementation.
